new_statements.rule_in_words: Primary stress falls on the penultimate syllable of the (root) word; suffixes and enclitics (e.g. plural -ro) and the paragogic /e/ do not shift it, so the stress domain is the root/stem and clitics are extrametrical. In vowel sequences (geminate vowels across a syllable boundary) the first vowel carries the stress. A cliticised word loses its final vowel and its primary word stress within a tight phrase or compound.
new_statements.exceptions: Suffixes, enclitics (plural /-ro/) and paragogic /e/ do not count for stress placement; cliticised words in tight phrases/compounds lose primary word stress (examples 22-23, p. 631). Author states the sketch describes the Masarete dialect unless otherwise noted.
new_statements.identity_note: The chapter is explicitly a sketch of the Masarete dialect of Buru (Buru Island, Maluku): 'Unless otherwise noted, "Buru" in this sketch refers to the Masarete dialect of Buru' (p. 625, per the extracted text). The catalog record 'Buru' (StressTyp2) is not dialect-specific; Masarete is the largest and the reference dialect (Grimes 1991), so the identity matches. A separate file already held by the project (Grimes_ERIC_ED384231, 'Digging for the roots of language death..') concerns Kayeli and Hukumina, distinct languages of Buru Island, and is not about buru1303.
